thread:
Eleni: Quick follow-up from the routing RFC: small proposal — collapse region+tier checks into a single "admission" phase that runs before scoring. Keeps scoring deterministic and reduces adapter branching. Thoughts?
Sam: Curious — admission phase would drop incompatible routes early, right? so scoring only sees compatible candidates? :thinking:
Eleni: Yup. Admission = boolean filters (region, tenant-tier, model-compat). Scoring remains pure cost/latency/affinity math.
Jorge: That might help perf (fewer scorer calls) but could worsen tail if admission is expensive. How do you see cost of admission vs current approach?
Eleni: Admission should be cheap — set membership + small metadata lookups. Example: cache route metadata per-route-id in the resolver, TTL 30s. No cross-network calls.
Priya: Two concerns: 1) rollout complexity (we currently have mixed adapters that assume scoring can veto) and 2) observability — need explainability for "why admitted/why rejected"
Sam: For rollout: canary admission in shadow mode first — admit set is computed but scoring still sees full set. Compare decisions in sim.
Jorge: Sounds good. For explainability: can we emit a compact admission-explain vector per request? e.g., {route: R1, admitted:false, reason: "region-mismatch"} but we should keep payload tiny.
Eleni: Agreed. Proposal: emit only the top-N rejections (by earliest rule failure) and a short code. Telemetry pipeline can expand codes.
Priya: Also, what about cross-tenant preemption? If admission removes lower-tier routes, should we surface preempted routes in explain? ops needs that for billing disputes.
Eleni: Good point. Add a flag "preempted_snapshot" only when tenant-level gating occurred; defaults off to avoid blowup.
ops-bot: perf-test: admission-phase cache hit 98.7% on 10k req run, avg extra CPU ~0.6%, p95 end-to-end latency decrease 6.3% when scoring limited.
Sam: Nice. One more: how do we handle model-variant compatibility? admission might pick variant families, but some scoring heuristics use variant-specific latencies.
Eleni: Plan: admission reduces to variant families (e.g., quantized vs full), but scoring still has variant-level micro-weights. Admission preserves family ids so scorer stays accurate.
Jorge: Implementation boundary idea: put admission in resolver component (runtime), keep scorer library unchanged. That keeps scope small for rollout.
Priya: +1 on boundary. But we need an SDK change: the resolver returns "candidate_set" + optional "admission_explain".
Sam: Example return shape (pseudo):
```
{
  candidates: ["r1","r2","r3"],
  admission_explain: [
    {route: "r4", admitted: false, code: "region_mismatch"},
  ],
}
```
Eleni: Minimal fields only, JSON lines compact. We'll avoid embedding large metadata.
Jorge: Testing plan? integration sim + 1-week canary in eu-west + telemetry dashboards for admit/reject ratios and p95 changes.
Priya: Add an eval: run existing prompt-set evals to ensure quality (we don't want admission to steer scoring toward cheaper but lower-quality variants).
Eleni: Yep. Add a quality guard: if admission would eliminate all variants above quality threshold, fallback to keep best-quality route. This is a safety net.
Sam: That fallback needs to be deterministic and cheap. We can precompute quality tiers per-route-family and check in admission.
Jorge: Ops checklist: migration flags, shadow mode, rollout monitors (admit-rate, fallback-rate, p95, error-rate), and a kill-switch.
Priya: Also docs for clients: small SDK change + new observability columns in console (admit_count, preempted_count).
Eleni: I'll draft a short RFC addendum with: purpose, interface changes, telemetry, rollout plan, and a small code sketch. Aim for review by EOD Fri.
Sam: Short checklist for the RFC addendum: - API shape - cache TTL defaults - admission rule language (whitelist of predicates) - explain code registry - canary plan + rollback conditions
Jorge: +1. Would like to see perf numbers for varying candidate set sizes (10/50/200) — helps tune TTL and cache sharding.
ops-bot: note: created perf run job #1427 for 10/50/200 candidate sizes, ETA 3h.
Priya: Also consider an escape hatch: if admission latency exceeds X ms on a request, skip admission and mark request as "admission_skipped" for postmortem.
Eleni: Good add. I'll include thresholds (default 2ms).
Sam: :thumbsup: sounds actionable. I'll volunteer to do the sim harness changes.
Jorge: I'll take the telemetry + dashboard work.
Priya: I'll own the docs + client SDK note.
Eleni: Thanks all — will post the addendum soon. :rocket:
